stem: A team needs Claude to call an internal inventory service exposed as a REST API. They want the capability to be reusable across several Claude applications and maintained independently of any one app. Which approach best fits?

options.text: Hard-code the inventory logic into each application's system prompt.
Build an MCP server that exposes the inventory operations as tools so multiple Claude applications can connect to it.
Paste the current inventory data into the context window on every request.
Rely on a built-in tool, since built-in tools can reach any internal REST API.

rationale: An MCP server exposes reusable tools that multiple Claude applications can share and that can be maintained independently.

why_wrong.A: Logic in a prompt is neither executable access nor maintainable across apps.
why_wrong.C: Pasting data gives no live access and wastes context on every call.
why_wrong.D: Built-in tools do not automatically reach arbitrary internal APIs.

source.excerpt: exam guide CCDV-F v1.0, seção 8 (amostra pública)

stem: Claude keeps calling your search_orders tool with the wrong date format and occasionally calls it when the user asks about invoices. What is the most effective fix?

options.text: A detailed description (purpose, when to use and not, parameter formats) plus a tighter input_schema.
Rename the tool to SEARCH_ORDERS_IMPORTANT so Claude prioritizes it correctly.
Remove the input_schema so Claude can send dates in whatever format it prefers.
Raise max_tokens so Claude has more room to reason about which tool to call.

rationale: Tool descriptions and schemas are the model's main guide for when and how to call a tool; detailed descriptions with explicit formats and boundaries reduce misuse.

why_wrong.B: Capitalization does not communicate purpose or format.
why_wrong.C: Removing the schema makes formatting errors more likely.
why_wrong.D: Output budget is not the cause of wrong arguments.

source.excerpt: Provide extremely detailed descriptions. This is by far the most important factor in tool performance.

stem: Your tool call to an external API fails with a timeout during an agent loop. How should the error be returned to Claude?

options.text: Skip the tool_result and start a new conversation with the same user request.
Return a tool_result for that tool_use_id with is_error: true and a clear error message.
Return an empty tool_result without an error flag so the loop can continue.
Add the error text to the system prompt and call the model again without a result.

rationale: Every tool_use needs a matching tool_result. Marking it is_error with a clear message lets Claude reason about the failure instead of acting on false data.

why_wrong.A: Dropping the turn loses all context and the pending tool call.
why_wrong.C: An empty success misleads the model into thinking the call worked.
why_wrong.D: System prompts are not the channel for tool results.

source.excerpt: is_error (optional): Set to true if the tool execution resulted in an error.

stem: You are packaging an MCP server that a developer will run locally as a subprocess of their desktop client. Which transport fits best?

options.text: stdio between the client and the local server process
Streamable HTTP behind a public load balancer
An email-based message queue between client and server
A shared database table polled every minute

rationale: stdio is the standard transport when the client launches the server as a local process; HTTP-based transports fit remote or shared servers.

why_wrong.B: Valid for remote servers but unnecessary overhead for a local subprocess.
why_wrong.D: Not an MCP transport and far too slow.

source.excerpt: Uses standard input/output streams for direct process communication between local processes on the same machine

stem: Your team repeatedly asks Claude to produce quarterly reports following a specific internal procedure, with templates and a helper script. No external system access is needed. Which customization fits best?

options.text: A Skill packaging the instructions, templates, and script, loaded when relevant.
A new MCP server exposing the procedure as a remote service.
Pasting the full procedure and templates into every conversation.
Fine-tuning a custom model on past quarterly reports.

rationale: Skills package procedural knowledge and resources that Claude loads on demand (progressive disclosure). MCP shines when Claude needs live access to external systems.

why_wrong.B: MCP adds a service to maintain without needing external access.
why_wrong.C: It wastes context and drifts across copies.
why_wrong.D: Heavy, slow, and unnecessary for a documented procedure.

source.excerpt: Unlike prompts (conversation-level instructions for one-off tasks), Skills load on demand, so you don't have to repeat the same guidance across conversations.
